solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Gas conflict on new labyrinthine network

parts.note: to gas or rabbit is to chatter idly
a war is armed conflict
re means on, in the sense of concerning

explanation.surface: Gas warfare breaks out across a newly laid maze of tunnels.
explanation.definitionFit: Burrows dug by colonies of these animals form a sprawling maze, so the phrase is used for any confusing network of passages.

clue.text: Turn cleaning tool to pickled fish

parts.note: to roll is to turn over and over
a mop is a tool for cleaning floors

explanation.surface: Someone abandons the housework and switches to preparing a fish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled-up fillet of herring marinated in vinegar is a classic pickled fish dish.

clue.text: Filleted and gutted ray having no moisture at all

parts.note: a filleted fish has had its bones removed

indicators.note: gutting a word removes its insides, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's ray, filleted and cleaned, has been left out until parched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' empties ray of its middle letter, leaving RY.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for completely parched, without the least trace of wetness.

clue.text: Hot-tempered Israeli running around caught by British

indicators.note: running around suggests letters scattered and rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An angry Israeli fugitive is finally captured by British police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running around' shuffles ISRAELI together with C and B.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone quick to flare up in anger is hot-tempered, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Throw away a stew which is cooked

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are mixed up like ingredients in a pot

explanation.surface: Someone discards a casserole that has been prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is cooked' rearranges the five letters of A STEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander or discard needlessly is to throw something away.

clue.text: Top lecturers first in debt! Endlessly terse

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for first goes inside the word for debt

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt
A is a first-class mark, as in A1

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A complaint that senior academics are both overdrawn and brusque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' trims terse to ERS. In British universities a Reader is a senior academic rank just below professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Reader is a senior UK university post above lecturer, so Readers are top lecturers.

clue.text: Settle elsewhere, good to leave Dubai, say

indicators.note: to leave tells us the letter for good is dropped out of the word

parts.note: to emigrate is to go and settle in another country

explanation.surface: Advice to someone thinking of quitting Dubai to settle in another country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes G from EMIGRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is one of the states of the UAE ruled by an emir, an example of the category.

clue.text: First ten PhDs swimming, they splash out regularly

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are floating about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A group of new doctoral graduates celebrates by going swimming and splashing about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges the twelve letters of FIRST TEN PHDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spendthrifts waste money freely, so they habitually splash out, an idiom for spending lavishly.

clue.text: Foodstuff from European (northern) with thanks

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A dish, apparently from northern Europe, served with gratitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Polenta is a cornmeal porridge from Italy, an example of a foodstuff.

clue.text: Son maintaining morning activity?

parts.note: having means holding or keeping, close to maintaining

explanation.surface: A son keeps up his morning routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing stubble with a razor is a typical part of many people's morning routine, an example.

clue.text: Carp about here? A place with absolutely no privacy

definitions.meaning: a bowl where carp-like ornamental fish swim around

definitions.text: A place with absolutely no privacy
definitions.meaning: a situation where everything one does is on public view

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the verb to complain, but it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass tank for pet fish is seen from every side, so the term describes life lived under constant public scrutiny.

clue.text: Eg, Bedouin can do … I'm wandering

indicators.note: wandering suggests the letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A desert traveller boasts of competence while roaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges CAN DO and IM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedouin are desert peoples who traditionally move from place to place with herds, an example of a roaming way of life.

clue.text: Stare closely at English and the old Globe

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of the
a globe is a ball, a sphere

explanation.surface: A theatregoer peers at Shakespeare's old Globe theatre in London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Globe' suggests Shakespeare's London theatre but is just a sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise someone at close range is to look them hard in the eye, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Ends with Yankee getting potted

parts.note: tips are pointed ends
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American finishes up by getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potted' looks like a plant in a pot, or a snooker ball sunk, but means slightly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Potted is slang for drunk, and tipsy means mildly intoxicated, a synonym.

clue.text: Reserve Antipodean informer — The Trial could be here?

parts.note: to book is to reserve
shelf is Australian slang for an informer

explanation.surface: An Australian informer is reserved for a courtroom trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Trial is Kafka's novel, so it might stand on a shelf of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel such as Kafka's work would be kept on a ledge holding volumes, an example-type cryptic definition.

clue.text: Money collected from Queen and Conservative

parts.note: off means away from, as in take it off the table
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Funds raised from the monarch and a Tory politician.
explanation.definitionFit: The collection of money taken during a church service is called by this name.

clue.text: Cook sat before a Sunday treat, perhaps

indicators.note: cook means to doctor or rearrange, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone sat down to cook a Sunday lunch beforehand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' rearranges SAT BEFORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional British Sunday lunch centres on a joint of oven-cooked beef, an example of a weekend treat.

clue.text: 'Arry's confusion and difficulty getting tropical fruit

indicators.note: Arry for Harry shows a Cockney dropping the initial H

parts.note: havoc is chaos and confusion
ado is fuss or difficulty

explanation.surface: Harry, a Cockney, gets into a muddle over an exotic fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: ''Arry's' signals dropping the H, as a Cockney would, turning HAVOC into AVOC.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped green fruit grows in warm tropical climates, an example.

clue.text: Where swingers swing in net without difficulty we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are to be judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a net is a trap for catching things; with ease means without difficulty

explanation.surface: Something caught in a net, easily, as people seem to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swingers' suggests partygoers, but these are circus acrobats.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats swing from a horizontal bar hung high in the circus tent, so it is where swingers swing.

clue.text: Catches snakes after end of March

indicators.note: after puts the snakes behind the letter from March
end of picks out the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: asps are venomous snakes

explanation.surface: Someone catches snakes once March is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes H from March.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasps are hinged metal fastenings, which are catches for doors and lids, a synonym.

clue.text: Whitney, for example, in US city

definitions.meaning: Whitney is the first name of the singer with this surname
a large city in Texas, home of NASA's mission control

explanation.definitionFit: The singer Whitney bore this surname, and it is also the name of the big Texas city.

clue.text: The colour of fresh clarets?

indicators.note: fresh suggests a new version, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A query about the shade of newly opened red wines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges CLARETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright red, an example of a colour.

clue.text: Turn, for example, answer on overly fine length of film

indicators.note: turn tells us the whole string of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: too means overly
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A film editor reworks an over-refined piece of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' reverses EG, A, TOO and F all together.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded film, measured historically in feet, so a length of film.

clue.text: To greater extent than usual some text rambles

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A complaint that a piece of writing goes on longer than normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks EXTRA from the words text rambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, the word means more than normally, as in extra careful.

clue.text: Something often crumbled? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: a stalk often baked under a crumble topping
an exclamation meaning rubbish or gibberish

explanation.definitionFit: The pink stalks are a favourite in fruit crumble, and the word is also slang for meaningless chatter.

clue.text: One going for birds in suit, like Bond, say

indicators.note: going for means one thing is replaced by another

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Aves is the biological class name for birds

explanation.surface: Someone who chases women while wearing a suit, in the style of James Bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birds' suggests women, but is the scientific class AVES replacing I in SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: James Bond is the epitome of polished charm, so the superlative of smooth fits him.

clue.text: Not in prison, female (unscrupulous) with a lot of money moving

parts.note: a released prisoner is out
low means base or unscrupulous

explanation.surface: A dodgy woman, freshly released from jail, is rich and on the move.
explanation.definitionFit: An outflow is money leaving an account or economy, so a large sum on the move.

clue.text: Confused anytime? Run to pound, say

indicators.note: confused suggests the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A muddled person asks whether to dash to the dog pound at any time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confused' rearranges ANYTIME and RUN TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The pound is the currency of the UK, an example of a unit of money.
